native_stages: Own C++ copy/assignment, truth/key preparation, sparse counts, size filtering, border clearing, sorted relabeling and sparse/dense map operations. Existing sole-core components label is the only native labeling provider.
runtime_metadata_providers: NumPy empty-array dtype admission/error policy, threshold conversion, dtype selection and scalar casting
Pinned deprecated-argument sentinel identity when scikit-image is installed; own sentinel when absent
Runtime NumPy metadata reshape warning policy
native_scope: The unchanged frozen real-dtype/layout/rank/threshold/output-state and returned-map assertions; defined morphology dtype rejection remains native and is not blanket-routed through fallback.
explicit_protocol_fallback: Array subclasses, custom array protocols, and non-base-array image/out/mask combinations use the existing explicit fallback policy. Base ndarray dtype rejection and partial mutation order remain in the native consumer shell.
unrepresented_scope: Exhaustive arbitrary object/complex/extended-precision consumer input and output combinations
Arbitrary object/complex/subclass ArrayMap constructor and mutation combinations
Undefined upstream out-of-bounds Cython map_array layouts

returned_arraymap.implementation: Own Python state shell and native map stages
returned_arraymap.contract: Returned sparse vectors, lookup/call, materialization, mutation, aliases, errors and lifetime are tested separately; the internal constructor is not a new public util/segmentation class.

sparse_safety: Huge int64 count/filter safety is native definition-level evidence only; no impractical original bincount or dense map allocation is attempted. Safe sparse relabel reference comparisons are separate.

workers.runtime: Same process-global sole _core state; scalar/SIMD parity profiles are separate

timings: None; public pipeline tests and corpus are untimed. Paths and passing contracts do not establish performance.
